compatibility.policy: This registry is the single source of truth for the hand-written SDK layers (transport, session, entitlement, preferences, runtime). It covers what ops/build/sdk-surface.json deliberately does not: the operationId surface is generated for TypeScript and Python only, so the hosted-login and commercial-entitlement behaviour of every published SDK is reconciled here instead. The checker never infers a capability from source; every present entry names the exact file and symbol that provides it, and every missing entry names the wave that will add it. A capability declared as parity must be present in every language, so closing a gap means flipping an entry from missing to present with a real symbol, not relaxing the declaration. Capability entries are append-only in id; changing the file or symbol behind a present entry is a deliberate edit the diff gate can review, and dropping an id or downgrading parity from parity to divergent is a breaking change for the cross-language contract and requires a minor version bump plus a CHANGELOG entry. Adding a language id is allowed and must declare every existing capability for it. A language is onboarded only after it has been reviewed against the parity floor; a language still onboarding must declare every capability so its debt is reported rather than hidden, but is not held to parity until it is onboarded. This exists so a newly added SDK is neither able to fake a pass nor able to downgrade a capability to turn the gate green. A capability may only become present in a language by implementing it in that language's SDK, never by a consumer reaching past the SDK to call the endpoint itself.

capabilities.summary: The HTTP transport is an injectable seam so a caller can supply retries, proxies, timeouts, or a test double.

python.note: W4: the seam is emitted by cmd/gensdk, so the generated client and the hosted-login facade share it. The default UrllibTransport refuses redirects, so a credential endpoint can never replay an authorization code, refresh token, or bearer at another host.

rust.note: W4: async Transport is the default; ReqwestTransport uses reqwest async, and the optional blocking feature adapts reqwest through spawn_blocking.

kotlin.note: Public context/store constructor overloads inject one normalized HTTP executor across OAuth, activation, preferences and authorization reads. OAuth wire types remain internal; the SDK retains PKCE, token validation, storage and refresh serialization. The shared response boundary validates status and UTF-8 byte limits even for injected transports. SnaplinkOkHttpTransport enforces no cookies, redirects or cache and a bounded call deadline. Covered by TransportInjectionTest and an external Android consumer compile.

capabilities.summary: Callers can branch on a usable session without issuing a request.

kotlin.note: A local point-in-time read only: no refresh, no request, no write, and no delete, so it can neither create nor resurrect a session. It shares one freshness predicate with accessToken(), so false at or inside the 60-second refresh skew means accessToken() would have to reach the network. Stricter than Go's IsLoggedIn, which ignores expiry. An unreadable record raises secure_storage_error instead of answering false, and the no-network, no-write, skew-boundary, and in-flight-logout cases are covered by sdks/kotlin/test/SessionQueryTest.kt.

swift.plan: Onboarding: review a genuinely local/no-network usable-session query with expiry and storage-error semantics.
swift.note: No dedicated local isLoggedIn query exists. accessToken() and currentSession() may refresh and are not equivalent. Native acceptance was not executed in cycle-02.

capabilities.summary: Identity, permissions, roles, and the menu tree are read through one typed call, and the permission-holding rule is implemented once by the SDK. A consumer that re-implements the rule will eventually disagree with the server and either hide a control it would grant or show one it would deny.

rust.note: W6: Authorization assembles /userinfo, /permissions/me, /roles/me and /menus/me. holds() mirrors domains/permissions/matcher.go exactly: domain:* is a PREFIX rule and a bare * is global.

typescript.note: The rule is asserted against ops/build/sdk-conformance/authorization.json, the same fixture Rust uses, so the two cannot drift.

python.note: Asserted against ops/build/sdk-conformance/authorization.json, the same fixture Rust and TypeScript use.

php.note: Asserted against the shared authorization.json fixture; authorize() on SSOClient supplies the authenticated request seam.

go.note: Asserted against ops/build/sdk-conformance/authorization.json, the same fixture Rust, TypeScript, and Python use.

kotlin.note: Assembles /userinfo and /permissions|roles|menus/me using the current bearer and the configured client_id, validating the response scope. Missing or malformed projections and endpoint failures propagate instead of empty success. Session-generation checks reject late reads after clear, logout or replacement login; projections are neither persisted nor cached. Permission matching is driven by all 13 cases in the shared authorization.json fixture; navigation recursively filters denied parents and buttons. Kotlin remains onboarding pending independent native/security and integration review.
